dedupe_keys.name: mine remote sensing datasets for scene classification and target detection hubei and jiangxi china

description: Two labelled image sets for machine learning interpretation of mine development from high-resolution remote sensing, built in Hubei and Jiangxi provinces in the middle reaches of the Yangtze River: a mine multi-scene classification dataset and a mine target detection dataset. The Zenodo record says the aim is to support assessment of disorderly and illegal mining and surface damage at regional scale, and describes a stereo attention model for scene classification and a multi-scale dual-attention model for target detection trained on the data. Published on 31 August 2023 by Weitao Chen, Zhenkun Hui, Wenxi He, Yuqian Zhu and Lizhe Wang, it holds two zip files of about 880 MB and 1.28 GB, free to download under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is two Chinese provinces. Caveats: image sources, class lists and dates are not stated on the page read, and it is a benchmark for algorithms, not a complete mine inventory. For simulation it gives training and test data for models that map active mines and mining disturbance, which can then feed exposure layers. Related catalogue records include the global ML-ready mining area dataset, MineNetCD and CUGMine.
